options: The layer consumers use to extract information for reporting
The layer that consumes or takes in data from source systems
The layer that stores pre-aggregated OLAP cubes
The layer that exposes data through APIs
The layer that archives removed data
questions.explanation: Despite its name, the Consumption Layer is the layer that consumes or takes in data from source systems; the layer consumers extract from is the Serving Layer.

questions.stem: Which layer is the Consumption Layer often confused with, because of its name?
questions.explanation: People assume the Consumption Layer is where consumers extract data, but that is the Serving Layer.

questions.stem: In Lambda Architecture, which layers are the Consumption Layers?
options: The Semantic Layer and OLAP Cubes
questions.explanation: In Lambda Architecture the Serving Layer is last; the Batch and Speed Layers, which process data from source to serving, are the Consumption Layers.

questions.stem: In a Data Warehouse, which zones make up the Consumption Layer?
questions.explanation: Within a Data Warehouse, the Consumption Layer is the Landing and Staging zone.

questions.stem: What happens in the Landing Zone?
options: The source data model is copied on an as-is basis
The data model is changed to business requirements
Technical data quality rules are applied
Data is exposed to end users
questions.explanation: The Landing Zone is where the source data model is copied as-is, without change.

questions.stem: Which example describes a rule applied in the Staging Zone?
options: Joining customer and sales tables into a star schema
Converting all date formats to one format and null values to a default
Deleting data after its retention period
questions.explanation: In the Staging Zone the data model stays the same but basic technical rules apply, such as unifying date formats, defaulting nulls and fixing numeric data types.

questions.stem: What kind of data quality rules are applied between the raw and processed layers?
options: No data quality rules at all
Technical data quality rules, not business data quality rules
questions.explanation: From raw to processed layer the rules are technical data quality rules, not business ones.

questions.stem: In which zone is the data model changed according to business requirements, as in a Data Warehouse or Data Mart?
questions.explanation: The Transformed Zone is where the data model is changed as per business requirement, for example into a Data Warehouse or Data Mart.

questions.stem: Which tool is named as one of the most used consumption tools for real-time processing?
questions.explanation: For real-time processing, Kafka is one of the most used consumption tools.

questions.stem: Why are CDC tools becoming popular in Big Data consumption layers?
options: Because they encrypt data in transit
Because they allow pulling only changed data from the source rather than a whole dump every time
questions.explanation: With huge data volumes, CDC tools let organisations pull only the changed data from source instead of a full dump on every load.
